question: How should root-owned scripts/reference-harness/report.ts and its gate.test.ts be scoped for reference block parity? The harness rejected both explicit extra consumer paths as lying under no module of the refreshed architect view, despite gd-001 placing root reference rendering in ramify.
requiredBehavior: The request requires the reference harness report script to display the same completed block as CLI full/changed, preserving its existing summaries. The CLI renderer can be exposed to its parent, but the root script and test must be writable by an engineer under a valid module scope without weakening test discovery.

findings.text: The script currently maps diagnostics to only a header in checkerSummary, while the CLI's shared findingBlock now builds complete blocks. The root test lives beside the script.

An assignment with base ramify/cli and exact extra consumer paths scripts/reference-harness/report.ts and scripts/reference-harness/gate.test.ts was rejected at submission: each path 'lies under no module of the refreshed view'. The accepted global placement explicitly called the reference script root-owned integration rendering; extra scope nevertheless cannot address it.

citations.note: Root script currently outside validated module scope.

candidates.note: gd-001 considers script root-owned but module-scoping validator does not consider its path part of ramify; need valid mapped ownership or a root entry work item.
Can expose a reusable block formatter from CLI, but cannot write the root script under its own module or accepted extra paths.

unresolved: A valid module scope for the root script and test, or a separate root-owned work item/authorized module proposal to render them without violating ownership.
Whether the CLI should export its existing formatter to parent for this consumer, pending a valid script scope.

hypotheses.evidence: Ownership by ramify is conceptually supported by script location, but the assignment validator reports root scripts are outside every module in the refreshed view; the forecast did not account for this scoping boundary.
The analysis diagnostic payload remains provider-owned and CLI can display it; root should only render, not compose evidence.
